top_story: Israel’s confirmed killing of Mohammed Odeh in Gaza City, after he had only recently replaced a predecessor killed earlier this month, shows a ceasefire coexisting with targeted decapitation strikes that keep Gaza unstable and signal Israel’s intent to disrupt Hamas’s command structure even during nominal restraint. In the West Bank, that pressure is mirrored in a more dispersed but socially corrosive form, as settlers backed by soldiers raided villages north of Ramallah, killed 16-year-old Yousef Kaabneh, and seized 900 sheep, deepening Palestinian insecurity through attacks on both life and livelihood. The same day, Donald Trump’s threat to “blow up” Oman if it aligned with Iran over the Strait of Hormuz landed as US-Iran talks stalled, sharply raising pressure on one of the Gulf’s key mediators and injecting fresh volatility into a vital maritime chokepoint. Taken together, these moves point to a region where coercion is overtaking diplomacy, widening civilian vulnerability from Gaza and the West Bank to the Gulf.
